Title: Formal PH-BN negotiations yet to begin, says PKR's Adam Adli
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional have yet to hold formal negotiations on cooperating for the upcoming Melaka state election, state PKR chief Adam Adli Abdul Halim said.
However, he said informal talks between both coalitions were ongoing through party representatives.
"At present, there are no formal negotiations at the state level anywhere.
"However, discussions with BN are constantly being held, either on an individual basis or through party representatives," he said on the sidelines of the Santuni Madani Bukit Katil programme.
Adam said political dynamics in Melaka had their own unique context and could not be compared with other states that previously held elections.
He said Melaka PH would evaluate all factors, including its experience in the state government, before determining its next move.
The coalition previously served in the state administration for three years before stepping back when its assemblymen withdrew over a constitutional amendment regarding appointed assemblymen.
DAP representatives resigned first before the coalition entirely withdrew from the BN-led state government.
"This is not a matter of having vast differences of opinion," said Adam.
"However, that three-year administrative experience had an impact on the community, especially in maintaining harmony and stability."
On whether DAP's withdrawal from the state administration would affect talks with BN, Adam said all factors would be weighed by each party.
"In any negotiation, I believe each party will have its own viewpoint and will need to bring something to the negotiating table," he said.
He added that state PH assemblymen were currently focused on completing their remaining duties before seeking a new mandate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Expand second-career opportunities for veterans, Wan Azizah urges private sector
Article:
SERI KEMBANGAN: The private sector needs to expand second-career opportunities for military veterans as part of efforts to strengthen their welfare and empowerment, said Kempen Tabung Pahlawan patron Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
She said the private sector also had an important role in ensuring military veterans were given opportunities to continue contributing to society and the nation after ending their service with the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF).
"I call on more parties to come forward and contribute to the Kempen Tabung Pahlawan, as well as veteran associations under the MAF Veterans' Affairs Department (JHEV).
"Every sen contributed will go directly towards the welfare and wellbeing of our national heroes," she said in her speech at the closing ceremony of the MyHeroes Golf Championship Cup 2026 (MYGCC 2026), organised by the Royal Malaysian Navy Veterans' Association (PVTLDM), here today.
A total of RM220,000 was raised from eight private companies through MYGCC 2026, held in conjunction with the Kempen Tabung Pahlawan, to support the welfare of military veterans.
Also present were Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Dr Zulhelmy Ithnain and PVTLDM president Commander (Rtd) Khairil Hariss Khairuddin, who is also MYGCC 2026 programme director.
Wan Azizah, who is also Bandar Tun Razak MP, said the government, through the MAF and JHEV, remained committed to safeguarding the welfare of military veterans and advancing their empowerment.
She said records showed that public and corporate support for the Kempen Tabung Pahlawan continued to grow.
"The contributions collected are used to support thousands of veterans and their dependants in terms of livelihood assistance, medical care, and education for the children of our heroes.
"This achievement is proof of the spirit of togetherness and the ethic of hard work without complacency, reflecting the principle of readiness to sacrifice that is upheld by every member of the Royal Malaysian Navy and the MAF," she said.

Title: Warisan exploring local alliances for GE, says Shafie
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Parti Warisan (Warisan) is open to working with local political parties that share its stance in championing the interests of Sabahans in the upcoming general election (GE).
Its president Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal said the party is currently exploring several approaches, including preliminary discussions with Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (STAR) and Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM).
He said any political cooperation must be based on principles, integrity and the interests of the people, rather than merely securing political positions.
"We are also holding preliminary discussions with local parties such as STAR and KDM to explore potential cooperation.
"Our priority is not merely political positions, but achieving the values and priorities of the people. Any political cooperation in the future must have clear red lines, be honest, uphold integrity and prioritise the welfare of Sabahans," he said during a press conference at the party headquarters today.
Shafie said Warisan is also fine-tuning its election preparedness strategy, including the possibility of contesting all 25 parliamentary seats in Sabah and one in Labuan.
He said Sabah currently has only 25 of the 222 parliamentary seats, making it important for all 25 seats to be represented by leaders capable of voicing the aspirations and interests of Sabahans.
"Sabah's members of Parliament represent only 25 of the 222 seats in Parliament. Therefore, it is crucial that all 25 seats are represented by leaders who genuinely carry the voice and aspirations of Sabahans," he said.
The former Sabah chief minister said cooperation among local parties is also important to ensure Sabah's interests can be more effectively championed at the federal level, including matters concerning rights enshrined in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and the Federal Constitution.
He said Warisan also recognises the common interests shared by Sabah and Sarawak as a basis for strengthening the Borneo voice, particularly on development and state rights.
Meanwhile, Shafie said Warisan is fine-tuning a new manifesto centred on the principle of "Sabah Voice, Sabah Rights" for the upcoming election.
He said Sabah's rights and needs must be given serious consideration by whoever forms the federal government after the election.
"Nation-building should not be based solely on race and religion, but on the needs of the people.
"The needs of people in Sabah, Sarawak, Johor, Kelantan and Terengganu are different. This diversity should be an agent of unity, rather than a source of division," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malay-Muslim unity must go beyond seat-sharing, says Annuar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation among Malay political parties should not be viewed merely as a seat-sharing strategy to win elections, says Perikatan Nasional (PN) information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa.
In a Facebook post today, he said such cooperation required deeper understanding and commitment to a broader political agenda, including the religious duty to unite the ummah, uphold Islam and champion the Malay community and the country.
"The unity of Malay-Muslim parties and their refusal to be divided will ensure genuine stability while enabling them to protect and champion the interests of all races, ethnicities and religions in the country," he added.
Annuar said Malay-Muslim leaders were expected to put religion, race and country ahead of factional or personal interests.
"Muafakat Nasional calls on all leaders to prioritise the understanding that has taken root, continue to nurture it and ensure it bears fruit," he said.
While he did not refer to any specific political issue, his remarks came as seat allocation talks between Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN are being closely watched.
BN and PN have yet to formally decide whether to cooperate in the upcoming Melaka election, including the allocation of state seats.
Earlier, PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the coalition remained open to negotiations with BN, including possible
seat swaps
, although no formal discussions had taken place.
However, several Umno leaders have made statements since last week signalling renewed BN-PN cooperation after the two parties secured a comfortable victory in the Negri Sembilan polls earlier this month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
Article:
KYIV: Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia's Belgorod region.
More than four years after the start of Russia's large-scale offensive against Ukraine, the two warring countries are ramping up long-range strikes, causing a growing number of civilian casualties.
Russia is relying on "ballistic terror," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at his country this week.
"More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed," he said.
The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, Zelenskyy.
Twenty-three people were also injured, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov. Images he shared show a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene.
According to the Ukrainian president, eight people were also injured overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings.
Zelenskyy condemned another "absolutely brutal" strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region.
Nine people, including four children, were injured there, he said.
Images posted on social media Saturday evening – which AFP has not been able to verify – show buildings on fire in what appears to be a commercial area.
In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region's acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev.
Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also injured, he added.
Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, according to him.
A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street.
According to the United Nations, the conflict has claimed more civilian lives this year.
The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled.

Title: 3,000 vehicles get Jalur Gemilang magnets nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 3,000 vehicles nationwide received free Jalur Gemilang magnets today under the Japen@Petronas Jalur Gemilang Expression Programme, held simultaneously at 15 selected Petronas stations in conjunction with the National Month celebrations.
Organised by the Communications Ministry through the Information Department, the programme is part of efforts to intensify the 1 House 1 Jalur Gemilang (1R1JG) Campaign, with strategic cooperation established with Petronas this year.
Under this year's expanded programme, Jalur Gemilang magnets were distributed to the first 200 vehicles at each participating station, bringing the campaign to fly the national flag closer to the public's daily lives.
In
KUALA LUMPUR
, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil attached a Jalur Gemilang magnet to a member of the public's vehicle at the New Pantai Expressway (NPE) Pantai Dalam Petronas station as a symbol of support for the 1R1JG Campaign.
Fahmi said the use of Jalur Gemilang magnets is an improvement this year following public feedback for a method that can be attached and removed easily without being permanently affixed to vehicles.
Meanwhile, in
KELANTAN
, state Information Department director Ahmad Ammar Othman said the magnets allow the Jalur Gemilang to be displayed neatly and safely on vehicles, making it easier for the public to express their patriotism on the road.
"We also held a handover of the Jalur Gemilang to federal and state government agencies, as well as the flag-off for the
Kembara Merdeka Jalur Gemilang X JAGO
convoy from Tumpat to Kota Baru, which will conclude on Aug 14," he said at the Chetok Petronas Station today.
In
NEGRI SEMBILAN
, state Information director Mohd Sabri Abdullah said the distribution aims to encourage the community to enliven National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations, while urging citizens not to wait until the last minute to fly the Jalur Gemilang.
"We will also intensify various ground and community programmes to raise patriotic spirit and public awareness on flying the Jalur Gemilang, including through the Jiwa@Komuniti Madani programme," he said.
In
PENANG
, a survey at the southbound Sungai Dua Petronas station found that most recipients were excited to receive the magnets distributed from 10.30am, describing the initiative as a welcome change from previous flag distributions and expressing hope that it would continue in the future.
State Information director Hasmiza Hussin said 14 staff members were involved in the programme, while efforts to enliven the celebrations would continue through collaboration with the state government and local communities, including flag distribution in several selected areas.
In
TERENGGANU
, private sector employee Puteri Izzatul Khaisara Che Hasnul, 34, suggested that the department increase independence-themed programmes and activities, particularly in rural areas, to foster nationalism among the public.
"Programmes like this should be held all the time, not just seasonally. Independence celebrations are no longer as lively as before. Flying the Jalur Gemilang at homes and shop lots has also decreased. The department's efforts are good, but they need to be strengthened," she said.
Meanwhile, in
SARAWAK
, state Information director Sabri Said urged the public to ensure that the Jalur Gemilang is displayed according to the correct protocol to prevent errors such as mounting it upside down.
He said that besides ensuring the symbols, colours and emblems of the Jalur Gemilang are correctly displayed, the public should exercise caution when using artificial intelligence (AI) so that generated flag images do not violate established guidelines.
In
PERLIS
, the programme at the Behor Temak Petronas station in Kangar received a warm response, with the public seizing the opportunity to obtain Jalur Gemilang magnets for their vehicles.
State Information director Aidatul Shima Che Hassan said the programme supports the nationhood agenda while broadening the reach of patriotic messaging and national pride among the community.
Similar programmes were also held in
KEDAH
and
PERAK
, with the Jalur Gemilang continuing to serve as a symbol of unity and patriotism during the National Month celebrations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Talks with US won't happen while interim deal is breached, Iranian FM says
Article:
DUBAI: Iran and the US are not engaged in talks and Teheran will not start them as long as Washington breaches an interim deal signed in June, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday, adding that messages are being exchanged via intermediaries.
Araghchi repeated Iran's position that an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz between Teheran and Muscat was in the "final stages" but would not reopen the strategic waterway.
In comments reported by Mehr news agency, he said the agreement would set out the new shipping lanes to be used once the US fulfils other conditions and the strait is reopened to traffic.
In another report, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Sunday said they would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US accepts all of Teheran's demands.
"Our current strategy is to maintain this strait until the enemy accepts all our conditions," said IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi, as quoted by state TV, adding that "the strait is now actually a theatre of war for us and not just a waterway".
Continued attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire.
Mediators have since urged both sides to return to the terms of a June memorandum.
Araghchi earlier said discussions with Oman over transit and management of the strait were "approaching the final stages", but added the reopening of Hormuz "is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation" of the June agreement.
Security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr on Saturday laid out a list of demands for reopening the strait, including an end to the "war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq".
He also demanded the lifting of a parallel US naval blockade of Iran, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage, according to remarks reported by Tasnim news agency.
IRGC also said Hormuz's reopening had "nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman", adding that the "enemy is forced to accept Iran's conditions for the opening of the strait".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shafie calls for stricter action against fake social media posts
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Parti Warisan has called for stricter enforcement of laws governing social media content following the circulation of unverified and false information involving the party.
Its president, Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal, said several fake social media posts had recently circulated, including claims that the party had withdrawn from the unity government following the outcome of the Negri Sembilan and Johor state elections.
He said a purported letter had also circulated claiming that he had asked the Sabah Immigration Department director to release an undocumented migrant from detention.
"That is absurd. I was a former deputy Defence Minister and I know the law. Why was the person detained, and why would I appeal for his release?"
Shafie said he had instructed the party's secretary-general to lodge a police report, while the party was also awaiting a report from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission before further action could be taken against those responsible.
"I hope it will not take too long," he told reporters at a press conference at the Warisan headquarters here.
He added that other fake social media posts had also circulated involving Warisan assemblymen, including purported wedding invitations and obituaries.
Meanwhile, Shafie said the party would hold its annual general meeting on Oct 31 in Sandakan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: Over 1,800 fake social media accounts detected, many playing up 3R issues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 1,800 fake social media accounts have been detected so far, with several used to spread race, religion, and royalty (3R) content, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said these accounts, primarily on Facebook and TikTok, often impersonate legitimate figures or organisations to publish false statements and trigger public backlash through gaslighting tactics.
"The majority of the fake accounts detected involved platforms such as Facebook and TikTok.
"We have observed that much of the 3R content originates from fake accounts," he said after officiating the Komuniti Kasih Madani programme at IWK Eco Park.
"Some accounts impersonated legitimate organisations or figures. They would publish a post, delete the account and the post, but screenshot the content beforehand to spread it as if it were authentic."
Fahmi said the ministry also observed a sharp rise in fake accounts fanning 3R issues, as well as those linked to online scams and gambling.
"The message we want to convey is that not everyone posting on social media is a real person," he said.
"Sometimes the name appears Malay, but the person operating it is not. Sometimes the profile picture looks like a man, but the operator is not."
He added that certain parties were also attempting to gaslight the public by issuing provocative statements to draw condemnation.
"We see certain parties attempting to gaslight the public," he said. "They intentionally publish statements to draw backlash, where the original poster is either a fake account or not a real person."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK observatory nervously watches growing space junk threat
Article:
IN the sweeping shadow of a satellite dish, staff at the Chilbolton Observatory in southern England track a growing number of objects in Earth's orbit, providing data that underpins Britain's space monitoring efforts.
As the hulking antenna swivels into action, screens inside the control room light up with the names of objects the radar system detects: stars, satellites and abandoned rocket bodies.
Experts at Chilbolton Observatory, operated by the UK's national space laboratory RAL Space, monitor UK-licensed satellites and fast-multiplying fragments of space debris swirling around them.
The space junk includes defunct man-made objects like rocket bodies, dead satellites and fragments from launches, explosions and collisions that threaten to re-enter Earth's atmosphere or crash into functioning satellites.
According to the European Space Agency, there are more than 46,000 pieces of debris weighing a total of 17,000 tonnes currently in orbit.
"Most of those don't collide with anything, most of the time," Matthew Archer, deputy director for launch and space domain awareness at the UK Space Agency told AFP on a visit to the observatory.
"But any of them can cause significant damage or even destroy potential satellites."
On Wednesday, part of a SpaceX rocket about the size of a bus slammed into the Moon, unleashing a stream of debris.
Researchers warn the growing density of space junk could trigger the so-called "Kessler syndrome" cascade of collisions.
Chilbolton Observatory feeds data to the National Space Operations Centre (NSpOC) – led by the UK Space Agency and UK Space Command – that works around the clock to prevent orbital collisions and track debris re-entering Earth's atmosphere.
"Our role is to look at everything that happens and is in space," said Archer.
Space infrastructure underpins some 20 per cent of the UK economy, said Archer. The growing "number of objects is making space far more congested, so the need for this capability is growing all the time."
There are currently 14,000 satellites orbiting Earth, with some 1.7 million satellites planned in coming years. SpaceX alone has unveiled plans to begin launching more than one million satellites in 2028.
The UK has pledged to invest £85 million (US$114 million) in the NSpOC, which issues around 3,000 monthly collision warnings to satellite operators.
[[nid:1507562]]
The researchers also monitor to ensure satellite operators are complying with their licences and track foreign "adversaries."
"We see examples of countries that have demonstrated the ability to get close or to fly by certain objects," said Archer. "We do have to track ... threats regularly from a military perspective."
And when space debris re-enters the atmosphere, scientists are on stand-by to issue alerts for objects which may not burn up before landfall.
In January, Britain and European countries closely watched the re-entry of a Chinese rocket, amid fears fragments could land in Britain. The rocket eventually splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.
"It really is a multinational environment and there are so many objects that are not controllable," said Chilbolton Observatory's facility leader Sarah Nash.
"The only way that all of this can continue to operate safely is by keeping track of where everything is," Nash told AFP.
Another branch of their work is planetary defence, which involves identifying threats like comets and asteroids.
Last year, the UK Space Agency became a member of the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), which monitors the movement of asteroids including those that could hit Earth.
"We work in partnership with NASA and others in the US to effectively give a percentage chance that (it) might hit the Earth and when that might happen," said Archer.
While smaller space rocks frequently burn up in Earth's atmosphere, large orbiting rocks like asteroids are rarer.
The UK to support the European Space Agency's 2029 mission to study a 375-metre wide asteroid called Apophis as it flies by Earth.
"Asteroids are a really interesting challenge in many ways. It's unusual for an asteroid to come out of nowhere," explained Nash.
The giant space rocks are generally monitored by optical sensors, as they are too far away for Chilbolton's radar dish to detect.
"If they're close enough for the (radar) antenna to see them, then we have bigger problems," laughed station manager Graham Marshall.
* The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN-BN pact could lift Perak win chances to 75pct, says Samsuri
Article:
TAIPING: Perikatan Nasional (PN) could see its chances of winning in Perak rise to about 75 per cent if it reaches an electoral pact with Barisan Nasional (BN), said PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
He said cooperation between PN and BN could also help the two coalitions win at least six state seats currently held by Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the next election.
Samsuri said PN's current chances of winning in Perak were estimated at 48 per cent.
He said the figure could rise significantly if PN and BN worked together, mainly because their votes would be combined and three-cornered fights could be reduced to straight contests.
Based on PN's analysis, he said a PN-BN alliance could win between 32 and 38 of the 59 state seats in Perak, while PH could secure between 21 and 27.
The six PH-held seats seen as having the strongest potential to change hands were Tualang Sekah, Hulu Kinta, Tebing Tinggi, Sungai Rapat, Hutan Melintang and Teja.
"The first is N.43 Tualang Sekah, which is currently held by PKR. That has the highest ranking.
"Second is N.24 Hulu Kinta, third N.26 Tebing Tinggi, represented by DAP, fourth N.44 Sungai Rapat (Amanah), fifth N.54 Hutan Melintang (PKR) and sixth N.46 Teja, which is currently a PKR seat," he said when opening the 23rd Perak Pas Convention at a hotel here today.
Samsuri said several other seats, including Sungai Manik, Changkat Jong and Sungkai, could also be won by PN-BN if their votes were combined.
However, he acknowledged that cooperation between PN and BN would not be easy.
He said one challenge was the possibility that some PN supporters might not vote for BN candidates, and vice versa.
Both sides would also need to carefully decide which party should contest each seat to avoid splitting their support, he said.
"If cooperation takes place, BN may ask to contest certain seats. This is where we need to look at our strengths and determine why a particular seat should be contested by us rather than others," he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Samsuri said PN and BN would need to adopt a "give and take" approach if they wanted to work together.
He said both sides should sit down and discuss their priorities, with the main aim of ensuring a stable government.
"As long as we can sit down and discuss, I think that is the best thing to achieve. The most important thing is to ensure the stability of the government that will be formed, whether at the state or national level," he said.
Samsuri also said political conditions differed from one state to another.
He said factors such as geography and local political dynamics must be considered when deciding how PN and BN would cooperate and divide seats.
"The political dynamics are very unique. They are not only time-based but also geographical-based. So, the model for each state will certainly be different. Until we sit down and decide, anything can happen," he said.

Title: Post-mortems in Johor, Negri find PH must do more to mobilise voters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A preliminary post-mortem into Pakatan Harapan's losses in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections indicates that the coalition must do more to mobilise voters, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
The PKR information chief said PH's problem in the polls did not lie in its attacking strategy.
"We have to ensure that our machinery remains focused on identifying voters and mobilising them on polling day," he said after officiating the Komuniti Kasih Madani programme at IWK Eco Park.
PH managed to win just eight of the 56 seats in Johor, down from the 12 it won in the 2022 election.
In Negri Sembilan, PH won only 11 of the 36 seats, resulting in it losing control of the state it had administered since 2018.
Fahmi, who is also PH communications director, said candidates must focus on introducing themselves and speaking about their plans for their constituencies.
"The machinery's focus is to engage voters and ensure those supporting the candidate and party turn out to vote.
"The candidate's focus is to introduce themselves and convey the message of what will be done for a particular seat or state constituency," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3 Rohingya men held over alleged sexual offence in Terengganu
Article:
KOTA BARU: Police have detained three Rohingya men to assist investigations into an alleged sexual offence involving a person with an intellectual disability in Kemaman, Terengganu.
Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said the case attracted public attention after a video showing a crowd gathering outside a flat in Kampung Enjin Gergaji, Chukai, near Kemaman, circulated on TikTok about 8.30pm last night.
"The gathering was believed to have started after the alleged sexual offence involving the Rohingya began circulating on social media," he said.
Mohd Khairi said the men, all in their 20s, were arrested after police received a report yesterday.
"So far, we have arrested three Rohingya men.
"Investigations are also ongoing to identify other suspects who may have been involved," he said.
He said the three men had been remanded for five days until Aug 12.
"The police need to thoroughly investigate the case, while the victim must also be given sufficient time as the person involved has an intellectual disability," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 376 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiong: Review crew screening to restore passenger confidence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aviation regulators and related agencies have been urged to review their internal management, security controls and risk prevention measures to ensure passenger safety remains assured at all times.
Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing also called for stricter screening of pilots and cabin crew before they begin duty, with checks carried out jointly by regulatory authorities and police.
He said aviation safety not only involved passengers' lives but also affected international tourists' confidence in the country's systems.
"Staff can be directed to report up to two hours before duty to undergo screening, if necessary. They should only be allowed to begin duty after passing the required screening.
"The relevant professionals can determine the type and scope of tests suitable.
"What matters most is that we have a more proactive and effective prevention method to prevent cases like this (drug smuggling) from recurring.
"All parties need to cooperate to close every gap, restore confidence in the aviation sector and protect Malaysia's image," he said in a statement today.
He was commenting on the case of a
Malaysian pilot detained by Indonesian authorities
on July 28 on suspicion of attempting to smuggle drugs.
The suspect was detained at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after 15 large packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills were found in his luggage.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) opened a regulatory investigation on Aug 2 into whether all aviation security requirements had been complied with before the
pilot departed
Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
Tiong also called for a review of airport screening and security systems, including equipment, procedures and inter-agency coordination, to better address current security challenges.
He said safety could not be taken seriously only after an incident occurred, but must be embedded in daily procedures, monitoring and operations.
"The recent case needs to be seen as a serious warning, not merely as an issue involving an individual, because it exposes weaknesses in the aviation system.
"Airlines and regulatory authorities remain responsible for ensuring there are no gaps in safety management, whether or not the staff member was flying the aircraft on the day in question," he said.
Tiong said the concern was not whether the person was flying the aircraft that day, but the positive drug urine test and weaknesses in monitoring.
"Passengers are questioning why Malaysia Airlines emphasised that the suspect was not operating the flight, instead of first apologising to the public and addressing the issue.
"This raises the question of whether there is an effort to downplay the seriousness of the case. Agencies and companies should not wait until an undesirable incident occurs before taking action," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ACCCIM wants 2027 Budget to ease cost pressures on businesses
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (ACCCIM) has called for the 2027 Budget to sustain domestic demand, strengthen household resilience and support businesses amid rising operating costs and intensifying competition.
Its president Datuk Ng Yih Pyng said the budget should also reinforce key growth drivers, sustain private investment momentum, enhance the structural competitiveness of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and strengthen Malaysia's export resilience.
"Businesses have had to navigate significant cost adjustments in recent years, including higher employment costs, the expanded Sales and Service Tax (SST), changes in electricity tariffs, rising energy-related expenses, and intensifying competition from foreign-run businesses," he said in his speech at the chamber's 80th annual general meeting.
Ng said ACCCIM had submitted a comprehensive set of proposals for Budget 2027, covering cost-of-living pressures, business operating costs, workforce productivity and skills development.
On taxation, he said the tax system should be further refined to support business expansion, reinvestment and cash flow management.
The proposals include raising the preferential tax threshold for SMEs, strengthening investment incentives such as the reinvestment allowance and investment tax allowance, and improving tax administration to provide greater certainty and flexibility.
"A more realistic CP204 tax estimation mechanism and a more efficient tax refund process would further support effective cash flow management and reduce compliance burdens," he said.
Ng said Malaysia must continue promoting high-value investments while strengthening domestic competitiveness.
"We propose extending the accelerated capital allowance until 2030, enhancing reinvestment incentives, and reviewing SME definitions to ensure mid-tier companies are not excluded from support measures," he said.
He also called for digital transformation to remain a key priority, with the digitalisation grant strengthened through a higher funding ceiling and greater flexibility to support phased technology adoption.
Ng said the government should also encourage the use of locally developed solutions and industry-specific technologies, while leveraging government procurement to strengthen domestic value creation through a structured "Buy Made by Malaysia First" framework.
The chamber also proposed reviewing the import duty de minimis threshold and requiring high-volume foreign online sellers with annual sales exceeding RM1 million to establish a Malaysian business presence with local representatives.
It also called for stronger product verification through certification mechanisms such as Sirim and the Malaysian Authenticity Portal.
Ng said food security should remain a strategic national priority, calling for a more integrated approach to developing Malaysia's agrifood sector.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PKR Youth calls for probe into RCI findings on Tabung Haji
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR Youth has called for a comprehensive, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Its vice-chief Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the call was in line with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia's, decree for enforcement agencies to track down those responsible "to the ends of the earth" to safeguard the integrity of the Muslim institution.
The Sungai Petani member of parliament said that while the RCI found allegations that TH assets had been sold to non-Muslims to be baseless, investigations and subsequent action should focus on three key areas.
"These include weaknesses in governance and political interference, shortcomings in financial reporting and loss recognition, as well as the distribution of hibah (profit distribution) that did not reflect the institution's actual financial position.
"The RCI noted the involvement of politicians in senior positions at TH and the influence of political considerations on key decisions. In the 2017 financial reporting, for example, TH reported a profit of about RM3.4 billion, whereas its actual position showed a net loss of RM1.4 billion after adjustments," he said in a statement today.
He said the disparity contributed to decisions to distribute hibah at high rates despite TH's strained financial position, ultimately weakening the institution's reserves.
In light of the findings, PKR Youth urged the Special Enforcement Task Force, comprising the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the police, to conduct an in-depth forensic audit to trace the flow of funds and bring those responsible for any breach of trust to justice.
Taufiq also called for the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on Aug 11 to provide a platform for a comprehensive and transparent debate on the alleged mismanagement.
"Those who have betrayed and damaged this institution belonging to the Muslim community can no longer hide behind their positions or political influence, regardless of which party they belong to.
"What happened to TH is not merely a case of ordinary financial irregularities, but a betrayal of the trust placed in it by the Muslim community," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Root decay, soil compaction caused Jalan Macalister tree to fall, says Penang city council
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Root decay, trunk cavity, chronic soil compaction and limited rooting space caused a 90-year-old Angsana tree to fall on Jalan Macalister today.
Penang Island City Council (MBPP) mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the 28-metre-tall Pterocarpus indicus tree had about 30 per cent root decay and a cavity hollowing out about 40 per cent of its trunk base.
"The combination of root decay, the cavity at the trunk base, chronic soil compaction, limited rooting space and the tree's height significantly increased the risk of structural failure," he told the New Straits Times.
The incident, which occurred about 9.10am in front of Tropicana 218 Macalister,
damaged a car and injured three people, including a 9-year-old girl.
The three victims were taken to hospital.
Rajendran said there were no reports of heavy rain or strong winds when the tree fell.
He said MBPP began clearing the fallen tree at 9.41am, and the road was reopened at 2.20pm.
The remaining debris is being cleared.
Rajendran said MBPP had assessed mature and aged trees along Jalan Macalister in 2024, resulting in 13 trees being felled.
"In 2025, a satellite remote sensing study for an early warning solution on tree health found the tree to be in good condition, with no warning indicators.
"The last tree maintenance work along Jalan Macalister was carried out on Jan 29," he added.
Rajendran said 148 of the 179 trees approved for removal this year had been  felled.
The trees were removed for various reasons, including blocked drains, dead or leaning trees, risk of falling, development projects, road and river widening, and involvement with Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP) pipelines.
Rajendran said MBPP would  continue  to assess trees  for safety, particularly those affected by infrastructure works and constrained rooting conditions.
"Following this incident, the department has instructed the appoinnted contractor to expedite work to reduce the height of trees and fell those with potential to topple along Jalan Macalister, based on assessments by certified arborists," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka PH open to political cooperation, eyes more state seats - Adly
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to negotiations with any party for the upcoming Melaka state election, said its chairman Adly Zahari.
He said the form of cooperation and number of seats to be contested have yet to be finalised, with two series of meetings held so far to assess the coalition's prospects, while preparations for the state election remain focused internally within PH.
"In a democratic political system, various forms of cooperation can be implemented. We are discussing, but we have not made any decision at the PH level.
"We have not finalised the form of cooperation outside PH itself, but we certainly welcome anyone who wishes to hold negotiations," he told reporters after launching the Bukit Katil Santuni Madani programme at the Melaka Tengah Vocational College field today.
He said the coalition has also not held discussions with Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN), but remains open to working with parties that share aspirations aligned with the core principles and values of the Malaysia Madani agenda.
Commenting on seat targets, Adly said Melaka PH is optimistic about increasing its number of state legislative assembly seats from the five seats it previously won out of a total of 28.
He said assessments are being conducted based on PH's strength in the three parliamentary constituencies it won, namely Alor Gajah, Kota Melaka and Hang Tuah Jaya, as well as its potential in Tangga Batu, Masjid Tanah and Jasin.
"Our primary focus is to increase our wins. We are very positive that we can indeed add to our core seats," he said.
Meanwhile, PKR state leadership council (MPN) acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said Melaka's political situation has its own distinct dynamics compared with other states forming the Unity Government, meaning all factors must be considered in any negotiations.
"Officially, there are no formal negotiations with BN yet, but communication and discussions are ongoing. Individually and as party representatives with BN, we will look for ways to resolve matters," he said.
Adam Adli added that for now, PH state assemblymen are focusing on fulfilling their duties and responsibilities to the public while avoiding excessive political polemics that could disrupt social consensus and unity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Sekolah Pondok' group calls on politicians to reject divisive rhetoric
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan Pondok Schools Association has called on political leaders to reject divisive political rhetoric, saying unsubstantiated claims about threats to the Malays and Islam could undermine national harmony.
The group was responding to Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang's recent remarks alleging that DAP, which he said now dominated Pakatan Harapan (PH), was continuing a colonial agenda aimed at weakening and removing Malay-Muslim political dominance in the country.
In a joint statement issued by the association's adviser Syeikh Wazir Che Awang Al-Makki and Zulkarnain Harun, the group said an allegation of such seriousness should be supported by clear and credible evidence.
It said political claims that were not supported by evidence could create suspicion and hostility, deepen divisions among Muslims and strain relations in Malaysia's multiracial and multireligious society.
"Such an approach to politics is contrary to the demands of Islam, which require justice, tabayyun (verification) and prohibit accusations without evidence," it said.
The group said Hadi's claim also appeared to overlook Malaysia's system of parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy, in which government powers are exercised within the framework of the Federal Constitution, Parliament and existing laws.
It pointed to Articles 3 and 153 of the Federal Constitution, which state that Islam is the official religion of the Federation, and the latter provides safeguards to the special position of Malays and natives of Sabah and Sarawak, alongside the legitimate interests of other communities.
"Therefore, portraying DAP's participation in the unity government as automatically enabling the party to abolish the position of the Malays and Islam is an inaccurate depiction of the country's constitutional and parliamentary framework," it said.
The association said that, from the perspective of siyasah syar'iyyah, politics should instead focus on public interest, justice, preventing harm and preserving peace rather than simply defining political allies and opponents.
It warned that fear-based political rhetoric might bring short-term political gains but could come at the cost of social cohesion and national harmony.
"Political differences are normal in a democracy. We can differ in terms of party, approach and views, but these differences must be managed with knowledge, facts, courtesy and justice," it said.
The group also called on political leaders, particularly those who carried the name and image of Islam, to exercise greater responsibility in their public statements.
It said leaders had a greater responsibility because their words could either help unite society or deepen existing divisions.
"Islam does not become stronger through slander. The Malays do not become stronger through fear. The country does not become stronger through division," it said.
The group urged political parties to move away from fear-driven rhetoric and focus instead on solutions to issues affecting Malaysians, including economic growth, the cost of living, employment, education and poverty.
Last month,
Hadi again launched a blistering attack on DAP,
claiming that the party had a "Chinese agenda" and was out to eradicate Malay and Bumiputera supremacy.
The Marang member of parliament said DAP intended to retain the meaning of Islam in the Federal Constitution based on the colonialists' interpretation, which upheld liberalism and freedoms espoused by the West.
Yesterday, Parti Amanah Negara Wanita chief Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said Pas must present its evidence through legal channels if it truly believed DAP and PH had an agenda to eliminate the Malays and Islam, or threaten the position of Islam in the Federal Constitution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ferrari driver: 'Think of your family before you act'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Ferrari driver allegedly assaulted by a Perodua Aruz driver in a viral road rage incident on the North-South Expressway (PLUS) yesterday hopes the man will change his ways and think about his family before taking actions that could have serious consequences.
Businessman Tiang How Soon, 40, said he had no intention of causing a commotion and that the incident occurred without any collision between the two vehicles.
He said the situation could have been resolved amicably without resorting to violence.
Tiang said the incident frightened his four-year-old son and believed the other driver's child, who was also in the vehicle, would have been similarly affected.
"I saw that his family was also in the car, including a young child.
"He should have been able to discuss the matter with me.
"For something this minor, is it worth assaulting someone and potentially going to prison? His family would suffer.
"I cannot comment much as police are investigating. As a father and someone with a family, I do not want his family to face problems because of this," he said at a press conference at the Selangor Dapsy Public Complaints Bureau today.
Recounting the incident, Tiang said he was travelling with his wife and son in a convoy heading to Melaka but fell behind after leaving a petrol station.
He said he was travelling at about 120kph when he switched from the right to the left lane to avoid a vehicle that had stopped suddenly in front of him.
"I tried to brake, but I was worried I would not stop in time and hit the car in front. I changed lanes to avoid a more serious accident.
"I saw the Aruz in my side mirror, about two or three car lengths away. I stopped in the middle lane and when the car arrived, there was no collision, but the driver became angry and shouted towards the passenger side of my car.
"I tried to explain that a car had stopped suddenly and that was why I had changed lanes, but he continued shouting.
"He was angry and swore at me. I asked him not to do so as I had a young child who was already frightened.
"I got out of the car and several people tried to help, but he suddenly assaulted me. He kicked and punched me in the face," he said.
Tiang said the incident, which went viral on social media, had led to negative perceptions about him and the motoring community, prompting him to explain what happened.
He said that he did not want to escalate the situation and that they had not been racing or driving recklessly, but were trying to avoid a more serious accident.
He said he had attempted to calm the situation and resolve the matter rationally, but the other driver was too angry and acted rashly.
Earlier, police said they were
tracking down the Perodua Aruz driver
who allegedly assaulted the Ferrari driver during the altercation on the PLUS highway.
Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya was reported as saying police received a report from one of the drivers involved at 6.40pm yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia can emerge as a global pioneer in Syariah-compliant digital finance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia possesses the necessary ingredients to be a global pioneer in Syariah-compliant digital finance, driven by the emergence of blockchain innovation and efforts to develop the world's first Syariah-compliant products within crypto banks, a global mobility entrepreneur said.
Singapore-based start-up company Multipolitan's chief executive officer, Nirbhay Handa, said Kuala Lumpur (KL) should carve out its own niche in the global digital asset ecosystem by leveraging Malaysia's established Islamic finance ecosystem.
This would be a better approach than competing directly with other international financial centres, he told Bernama in an interview recently.
He said Malaysia should also focus on building greater institutional participation in the digital asset ecosystem rather than relying primarily on retail investors.
This is especially so given that KL emerged among the global top 10 cities in a comprehensive ranking under Multipolitan for its Crypto Friendly Cities Index 2026, published on its lifestyle and wealth advisory platform in June this year.
The ingredients favouring Malaysia's potential to be a pioneer in Syariah-compliant digital finance include the availability of certified digital assets, specialised exchange accounts, asset-backed tokens, crypto mutual funds and non-interest staking protocols.
These products are halal as they avoid interest, excessive gambling-like speculation, high uncertainty and involvement in prohibited industries.
Co-founded in 2024 and backed by unicorn tech entrepreneurs, Multipolitan is a start-up company that provides a product-driven global migration and international mobility platform aimed at modernising the complex, bureaucratic immigration industry through a frictionless, software-driven experience.
"KL can have a niche-wide, mile-deep philosophy and remain a front-runner when it comes to Islamic finance," he said.
Handa said Multipolitan is also exploring Malaysia as part of its expansion plans, noting that beyond Islamic finance, KL is well-positioned to become a regional hub for shared service centres due to its strategic location, access to skilled talent and competitive operating costs.
Describing Malaysia's geography as the "ultimate hedge" in the current global environment, Handa said the country offers companies access to quality talent at a moderate cost, making Malaysia's capital city an attractive base for regional operations.
Institutional Participation Key to Digital Asset Growth
Elaborating, Handa said Malaysia should focus on building greater institutional participation in the digital asset ecosystem to unlock broader economic benefits, rather than relying primarily on retail investors.
A retail investor is an individual, non-professional person who buys and sells stocks, bonds, or funds with their own personal money.
He said retail investors tend to be more speculative and are more likely to enter during bull markets and retreat during downturns.
"Institutional investors are in it for the long term. If Malaysia wants to benefit from Web 3.0, it needs to attract institutional investment into digital assets," he said.
Web 3.0 refers to the next generation of the internet powered by blockchain technology, enabling decentralised applications, digital assets and tokenised services.
He added that greater institutional adoption would help create high-value jobs and strengthen the digital asset ecosystem by attracting market makers, fund administrators and compliance professionals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN open to seat talks, swaps with BN for Melaka polls
Article:
TAIPING: Perikatan Nasional (PN) is keeping the door open for negotiations with Barisan Nasional (BN), including possible seat swaps, as political parties gear up for the Melaka election.
PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said although no formal discussions had taken place, there was still ample time for both sides to explore possible electoral cooperation before the Melaka state legislative assembly is dissolved.
He said PN was also prepared to engage with its Muafakat partners should there be willingness from all parties to negotiate.
"PN is open to any negotiations, which have yet to take place at this point.
"With the time available, there is ample room for parties within PN to sit down and discuss, as well as with other Muafakat partners.
"If BN is ready to discuss, InsyaAllah, we are also ready to discuss," he told reporters after opening the 23rd Perak Pas Convention at a hotel today.
Samsuri said it would be more ideal for discussions to take place before the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly, allowing all parties sufficient time to prepare for the polls.
He said political developments in Johor and Negri Sembilan had demonstrated two different models of cooperation, which could be considered in determining PN's approach in Melaka.
"Many things can happen. We have seen what happened in Johor and what happened in Negri Sembilan - two different models.
"As for what will happen in Melaka, we will see when the time comes," he said.
Yesterday, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr
Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
said the party remains open to negotiating seat allocations for the upcoming Melaka election, including seat swaps.
Zahid, however, said any negotiations must be conducted in good faith and should not result in parties giving up seats they had previously won.
The deputy prime minister said BN had not completely closed the door to negotiations, but there must be limits to protect the interests of the parties and the seats they had won.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TA Securities sees Bandar Bukit Raja driving Sime Darby Property growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd's (SD Property) Bandar Bukit Raja (BBR) township could become a more meaningful contributor to the group's development and recurring income, TA Securities said.
The firm said a recent visit to BBR provided greater visibility into SD Property's second flagship growth corridor and its transformation from a predominantly residential township into a more diversified residential, commercial and industrial ecosystem.
"The visit complements our earlier Elmina trip but highlights a different aspect of SD Property's transformation.
"Elmina highlighted the group's newer data centre and build-to-lease pipeline, while BBR reflects its longer industrial evolution from land sales to ready-built factories, built-to-suit solutions and institutional logistics assets," it said in a note.
Spanning 2,158 hectares (ha), BBR has about 445ha of land remaining, with a gross development value of RM14.4 billion.
Industrial and commercial components account for 68 per cent of the remaining land area.
TA Securities said the 399ha BBR Business Park is the immediate growth driver, while E-Metro Logistics Park demonstrates SD Property's ability to combine its own investment with institutional capital to scale up its income-generating assets.
It said SD Property's industrial development at BBR has expanded steadily since the launch of its first industrial phase in 2011.
BBR1 introduced ready-built semi-detached, detached and affordable factories, while BBR2 marked a broader industrial expansion, with all 57 built-to-suit lots sold within a day.
The phase also attracted RM700.5 million in investment for Vinda SEA's hub and later anchored a RM1 billion industrial development fund with LOGOS Southeast Asia.
TA Securities maintained its "Buy" call on SD Property, with an unchanged target price of RM2.10.
"The visit reinforced our view of SD Property's medium-term industrial and recurring income growth.
"BBR Business Park provides a sizeable development pipeline, while E-Metro Logistics Park and the fund platform allow the group to expand its income-producing portfolio without fully funding the assets on balance sheet," it said.

Title: SLP Resources' strong profitability seen extending into Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SLP Resources Bhd's strong profitability is expected to continue into the third quarter of financial year 2026 (FY26), despite challenging demand for plastic packaging products in Malaysia amid persistent domestic competition, Kenanga Research said.
The research firm said higher resin prices year-on-year would support higher selling prices, translating into higher absolute profits even if the cost-plus margin remained steady.
It expects margins to benefit for another quarter or two from lower-cost inventory purchased earlier, while improving global market sentiment could provide a catalyst for the packaging sector following a low base in FY25.
Kenanga Research forecasts the ringgit at between RM3.88 and RM3.95 against the US dollar in 2026, which should limit the impact of unfavourable foreign exchange translation compared with FY25.
"The group will likely not suffer from unfavourable forex translation in FY26 as much as in FY25," it said.
It also forecasts Brent crude oil prices to average US$80 a barrel in 2026 and US$74 in 2027, noting that prices are unlikely to return to pre-war levels even if tensions in the Middle East ease.
"On that note, SLP Resources appears to be able to get sufficient resin supplies from well-diversified sources across the world, underpinned by its strong cash position," it said.
Kenanga Research said another key earnings catalyst is the ongoing development of medical-related components and devices for several international clients, which command above-average margins.
It expects Japan to remain SLP Resources' largest export market, accounting for more than 40 per cent of its plastic packaging sales.
The firm maintained its "Outperform" call on the company with a target price of 90 sen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Let's work towards digital sovereignty
Article:
LETTERS:
Malaysia is fast becoming Southeast Asia's data centre darling. Billions in foreign investment are pouring into Johor, Selangor and the Klang Valley as tech giants set up shop.
Our strategic location, reliable infrastructure and business-friendly policies have made us attractive.
The bigger challenge isn't physical, it's intellectual. We cannot be content hosting foreign servers while importing AI models, software platforms and digital expertise from elsewhere.
True, digital sovereignty demands that we build our own AI capabilities, strengthen local software industries, develop semiconductor talent, invest in cybersecurity innovation and pour serious resources into research and development.
Let's not forget the data itself. The government records, healthcare information, financial transactions, strategic national databases — these need robust protection under strong governance frameworks.
Data is now the world's most valuable resource and safeguarding it is a matter of national security, not just IT policy. Additionally, we need a workforce ready for the AI economy.
Universities must expand programmes in artificial intelligence, cloud engineering, cybersecurity, semiconductor design and digital ethics.
Technical and vocational institutions should equip young Malaysians with practical, hands-on skills to manage and innovate in this fast-moving sector.
Energy policy must evolve in lockstep with digital expansion. Every new data centre should be pushed to maximise renewable energy, improve efficiency, recycle cooling water and minimise environmental harm.
Green data centres should become the standard, not the exception. We also need to make sure local companies get a real seat at the table.
Incentives shouldn't just lure multinationals, they should nurture Malaysian tech firms, AI startups and innovative entrepreneurs.
A vibrant domestic ecosystem creates better jobs and reduces our long-term reliance on imported technology. Strong governance is essential, too.
Clear policies on AI ethics, cybersecurity, cross-border data flows and critical digital infrastructure will maintain public trust while encouraging innovation. Policies must be coordinated across ministries.
A respected digital nation is when we own the knowledge, control the technology, able to protect the data and share fairly in the prosperity generated.
K. TAMIL MARAN
Seremban, Negri Sembilan
The views expressed in this article are the author's own and do not necessarily reflect those of the New Straits Times

Title: Islamic outreach body backs King's call for thorough TH probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Islamic Dakwah Foundation (Yadim) supports the decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, calling for a comprehensive, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), as well as firm action against any legal violations.
Its president Datuk Dr Hasan Bahrom said the RCI findings should not merely be made public but thoroughly examined by the relevant authorities to address identified weaknesses and ensure any breaches of the law were dealt with through established procedures.
He said TH, as the institution entrusted with managing Muslims' savings for the haj pilgrimage, must be strengthened through transparent governance, effective internal controls and compliance with Syariah principles.
"Yadim hopes the follow-up to the RCI report will be carried out professionally, based on facts and the rule of law, without turning the issue into a platform for political gain or baseless accusations.
"What matters most after the report is released is the action that follows," he said in a statement here today.
Hasan said Yadim supported appropriate action on substantiated findings and efforts to rectify identified weaknesses to safeguard the Muslim community's trust in TH.
He also supported the position of Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan that the RCI findings should serve as a basis for improving TH's governance.
Yesterday, Sultan Ibrahim decreed that investigations into the RCI report on TH must be conducted thoroughly, with no stone left unturned. https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2026/08/1506640/updated-king-no-guilty-party-should-escape-action-over-th-felda-issues
His Majesty said the move was crucial to ensure all parties found responsible faced appropriate action and to prevent similar issues from recurring.

Title: Bersatu still in PN, says Samsuri
Article:
TAIPING: Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) remains a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN), says PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, despite claims that its membership had been revoked.
He said no decision had been made to remove Bersatu from the coalition and its status remained unchanged as of today.
"As of today, Aug 9, Bersatu is still a member of Perikatan Nasional.
"Although Bersatu's position in PN is somewhat unique, there have been reports that several of its MPs have lodged complaints with the Registrar of Societies (ROS) questioning the legitimacy of the party's leadership."
"Therefore, we also want to see the extent to which that legitimacy is being questioned by ROS. For now, they remain members of PN," he told reporters after opening the Perak PAS 23rd Convention at a hotel here today.
Asked whether PN would convene a meeting to discuss Bersatu's position, Samsuri said its priority was preparing for the upcoming Melaka election and the next general election.
"I believe the number one priority in PN right now is to ensure we win as many seats as possible in the Melaka election, which is the most immediate concern, and certainly at the federal level.
"So there is nothing else on the agenda to be discussed," he said.
On reports that Bersatu leaders intended to refer the matter to ROS following disagreements over the party's position within PN, Samsuri said they were free to take any action they deemed appropriate, provided it complied with the law.
"Our country is independent and has rules and laws that have been established.
"So it is up to them what steps they want to take, as long as they comply with the provisions of the Constitution and the law," he said.
On criticism against him, including allegations that he had become a "puppet", Samsuri said he would not interfere with what others chose to say.
"It is up to them. I cannot stop them from saying whatever they want. They have the right to say whatever they wish," he said.
On Friday, Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang claimed that Bersatu's membership in PN had been automatically revoked following its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's announcement that the party would form a
new coalition
.
Hadi, who is also Marang MP, said the move was in line with the coalition's constitution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ideas, Bersih call for transparent constituency fund allocation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to ensure constituency development funds (CDF) are allocated transparently and fairly, regardless of political affiliation, amid reported restrictions on MPs' access to the MyKhas platform.
The Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (Ideas) and Coalition for Clean and Fair Elections (Bersih) said CDF should not be used as a political tool or a form of reprimand against elected representatives.
They said the restriction of Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail's MyKhas access, following similar restrictions involving Subang MP Wong Chen and Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung, highlighted wider concerns over CDF administration.
In a joint statement today, the groups called for CDF to be codified in law and distributed through a transparent, formula-based system based on constituency development needs and population size.
They also called for detailed CDF guidelines and circulars to be made publicly accessible, with reports on the use of allocations disclosed to strengthen transparency and accountability.
Ideas chief executive officer Aira Azhari said the federal and state governments should ultimately move away from distributing CDF through elected representatives.
"Elected representatives should focus on their legislative, policymaking and check-and-balance role in holding the Executive to account," she said.
She said welfare aid and minor local projects should instead be administered objectively by government agencies.
On Aug 6, Lee, whose MyKhas access was barred in May, claimed
public funds allocated
to his constituency of Petaling Jaya were being channelled through PKR Petaling Jaya division chief Hee Loy Sian.
Meanwhile, Bersih chairman Faisal Aziz said distributing CDF through elected representatives could allow the Executive to exert unnecessary pressure on lawmakers and could also be exploited for political purposes.
He reminded Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim that Pakatan Harapan had previously pledged to provide equal allocations to all MPs regardless of political affiliation.
The groups said the current system created an "anti-competitive political environment" and stressed that the Executive must not "weaponise" CDF for political ends.
Yesterday, five PKR MPs said restricting an MP's MyKhas access further
blurred the distinction
between the party and government, as well as between democracy and autocracy.
In response, PKR Information Chief and unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MyKhas allocations were the Prime Minister's Special Allocation, as stated in Malaysia Plan and Budget documents, with the distribution mechanism determined by the Prime Minister.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Accused Thai school shooter had watched violent content online
Article:
BANGKOK: The Thai teen behind a deadly school shooting outside Bangkok had an air gun confiscated by a teacher last year and had watched violent content online, police said on Sunday, as the government promised new safety protocols for schools.
As investigations continued into Friday's rampage, where a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot dead his grandparents at home before killing another six people at his school before turning the gun on himself, police said the boy had used social media to learn how to use a firearm.
"According to witness interviews, the perpetrator had begun showing interest in studying the use of firearms for some time, about one to two years," Atthapol Anusit, deputy commissioner of the Provincial Police Region 1, told reporters.
Atthapol, who said police had so far interviewed 17 witnesses, said a knife had also been found in the boy's bag and other evidence found at the crime scenes included a firearm, spent cartridge cases, and a personal computer.
"After examining the PC, it was found that the child had watched social media content involving violence," the deputy commissioner said, but added there was no evidence yet that he had practiced shooting.
He said that last year a teacher had confiscated a BB gun, a type of air gun, that the boy took to school. The boy had lived with his grandparents for 12 years after his parents had separated, Atthapol said.
The Ministry of Education said it would develop new safety protocols over the next three months, including mental health screenings and a system to refer at-risk people to specialists, drills for emergency response plans, a drive to stamp out bullying and better detection to stop items from being taken into schools.
Along with those who died, more than 20 people were injured in Thailand's worst mass shooting since 2022, which has reignited debate over firearms control in Southeast Asia's largest gun-owning nation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taylor Swift songs removed from White House, Trump campaign posts
Article:
WASHINGTON: Some Taylor Swift songs have been removed from social media videos posted by President Donald Trump's campaign and the White House, which has used two of the American superstar's songs over the past week.
The White House and a representative for Swift did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Swift has not spoken recently about Trump, although she endorsed his Democratic rival, then-Vice President Kamala Harris, in 2024.
During the 2020 campaign, Swift posted on social media that Trump was "WELL AWARE we do not want him as our president."
Trump has repeatedly criticised Swift. After she endorsed Harris, the Republican said on social media, "I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT!"
Last year he wrote: "Has anyone noticed that, since I said 'I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT,' she's no longer "HOT?"
Dozens of artists, including Sabrina Carpenter and Ariana Grande, have called on the Trump administration not to use their songs.
The Trump campaign used two Swift songs over the last week on its TikTok page.
One, playing on her lyrics, featured the caption: "Red (Donald Trump's Version). Red (Taylor Swift Wrote A Whole Album About Republicans). Donald Trump. Everything Has Changed (At Our Southern Border). Donald Trump. We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together (The Biden Harris Administration). Donald Trump. The Last Time (An Autopen Runs The Country)."
It referenced famous songs by the pop star.
In June, Trump's campaign posted a video on the short-video platform with Swift's new "Toy Story 5" song "I Knew It, I Knew You."
The short video was captioned "Nobody loves our country & the American People more than @President Donald J Trump."
It showed him interacting with children at the White House, dancing at a UFC match and appearing at a rally.
It was the third time the Trump administration or his campaign had used one of the Grammy Award-winning pop star's songs in recent months.
In April, the White House shared a video showing the crew of Artemis II meeting with Trump at the White House the day before.
The video used Swift's "High Infidelity" and lyrics from the song: "Do you really want to know where I was April 29th?"
The White House shared another TikTok video in November featuring "The Fate of Ophelia" from Swift's "The Life of a Showgirl" album, which had been released the month before.
That video featured images of the US flag, monuments and various photos of Trump, including his 2023 arrest mugshot.
That post garnered widespread social media reaction and led to a White House spokesperson telling multiple news outlets the video was created because the Trump administration knew news outlets "would breathlessly amplify them."
The communications team for Trump, who is prolific on social media, has posted an array of hit songs with images including Trump's immigration crackdown, US military operations against Iran and the arrest of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.
